title: Add a fines feature and an overdue report to a Java library app
prompt:
This library app has three features, each a package under com.example.library: catalog (Book, Category and Catalog: books and their daily fine rate in cents), members (Member, Tier and Directory: standard and student members) and loans (Loan and LoanRepository: who borrowed what, with due and returned dates). The layout is package per feature: a feature's public API is the public classes in its top package (for example com.example.library.loans); its internals live in subpackages (.domain, .adapters) and are never used from outside the feature. FeatureBoundariesArchTest checks that. Add overdue fines as a new feature in the package com.example.library.fines with the same layout, and an overdue report command.

The fines package has a public final class Fines with the static method long fineCents(FineInput input), and a public record FineInput(long dailyRateCents, long daysLate, Tier tier) (Tier is com.example.library.members.Tier), plus whatever LibraryApp needs. The fine for one loan is daysLate times the book's daily rate, capped at 20 times the daily rate (the cap applies before any discount). Students pay half of that, rounded down to a whole cent. All money is whole cents.

The overdue report covers every loan in the app's seeded data as of a date given by the caller (an ISO date such as 2026-03-31; never read the clock). A loan is late by the number of days its end date is after its due date, never negative. The end date is the return date when the loan was returned on or before the as-of date; a loan returned later than that (or not returned) is still out, so its end date is the as-of date. A loan returned late therefore keeps its final fine however far in the future the as-of date is. The fine of each loan comes from its book's daily rate (use the catalog's rate, do not copy the rate table) and its member's tier; loans whose book or member does not exist are ignored. A member's total is the sum of their loan fines.

Add the command overdue <asOf> to LibraryApp.run, next to catalog, loans and member-loans, so that LibraryApp.main reaches the new feature: the gate fails production classes that only tests use. The command writes through the Output it is given, each line ending with a newline. The first line is "Overdue fines as of <asOf>". Then one line per member whose total is more than zero, formatted "<member name>: $<dollars>.<cents>" with two digits of cents (for example "Ada Stone: $12.50", "Edgar Dunn: $0.05"), ordered by total descending, then by name ascending (String order). When no member has a fine, the second line is "No overdue fines".

Use the catalog, members and loans features only through their top packages; do not change those features. Add tests in src/test/java/com/example/library/fines/FinesTest.java. Run nitpicker-gate until it exits 0.
